source_text: Χρὴ δὲ ἔτι νέον ὄντα φοβεῖσθαι Θεὸν, πρὶν ἢ ἑαυτὸν παραδοῦναι κακοῖς, πρὶν ἐλθεῖν τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ μεγάλην ἡμέραν καὶ φοβερὰν, ὁπότε ἥλιος μὲν οὐκέτι λάμψει, οὐδὲ σελήνη, οὐδὲ οἱ λοιποὶ ἀστέρες, κινηθήσονται δὲ αἱ ὑπέρτεραι δυνάμεις, ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ ὅλων χειμῶνι καὶ ταράχῳ, οἱ κοσμοφύλακες ἄγγελοι· ὡς παύσασθαι μὲν ἄνδρας δυνάστας, παύσασθαι δὲ καὶ γυναῖκας ἐργαζομένας, φευγούσας εἰς τὰ σκοτεινὰ τῶν οἰκημάτων, κεκλεισμένων ἁπασῶν τῶν θυρῶν· καί τις γυνὴ τοῦ ἀλήθειν ἀποσχομένη διὰ τὸ δέος, ἰσχνοτάτῃ φωνῇ χρήσεται ὥσπερ λεπτότατον ὄρνεον· ἅπασαι δὲ ἄναγνοι γυναῖκες εἰς γῆν πεσοῦνται, καὶ πόλεις καὶ αἱ τούτων ἀρχαὶ αἱ μιαιφόνοι, περιμένουσαι τὴν ἄνωθεν κόλασιν, ἐνστάντος καιροῦ πικροτάτου καὶ αἱματώδους, ὥσπερ ἀνθοῦντος ἀμυγδάλου καὶ συνεχῶν ἐπικειμένων κολάσεων, ὥσπερ πλήθους ἐφιπταμένων ἀκρίδων, καὶ ἐκποδῶν ῥιπτουμένων τῶν παρανόμων, ὥσπερ μελαίνης καὶ εὐκαταφρονήτου καππάρεως. Καὶ ὁ μὲν ἀγαθὸς ἀνὴρ εἰς αἰώνιον οἶκον τὸν ἑαυτοῦ χαίρων πορεύσεται· οἱ δέ γε φαῦλοι, πάντα τὰ αὐτῶν ἐμπλήσουσι κοπτόμενοι, καὶ οὔτε ἀργύριον ἀποτεθησαυρισμένον, οὔτε χρυσίον δόκιμον ἐπωφελὲς ἔτι. Μεγάλη γὰρ ἅπαντα καθέξει πληγὴ, καὶ μέχρις ὑδρίας ἑστώσης πρός τινι κρήνῃ, καὶ τροχοῦ ὀχήματος, ὃν ἂν τύχῃ καταλελεῖφθαι ἐν τῷ κοιλώματι παυσαμένης, χρόνον τε περιδρομῆς, καὶ τῆς δι᾽ ὕδατος ζωῆς παροδεύσαντος τοῦ λουτροφόρου αἰῶνος. Ἀνθρώπων δὲ ἐπὶ γῆς κειμένων μία σωτηρία, εἰ ἐπιγνοῖεν αὐτῶν αἱ ψυχαὶ, καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀναπταῖεν ὑφ᾽ οὗ καὶ γεγέννηνται.
thought_title: Call to fear God before the great day of judgment
orientation: Solomon continues his address, urging the young to fear God before the terrifying day of the Lord arrives, describing cosmic upheaval, the collapse of human power, and the final separation of the good and the wicked.
pass_a_gloss: But it is necessary, while still being young, to fear God, before handing oneself over to evils, before the great and fearful day of God comes, when the sun will no longer shine, nor the moon, nor the rest of the stars, and the higher powers will be shaken, in that winter and turmoil of all things, the world-guarding angels; so that mighty men cease, and also working women cease, having fled into the dark places of the dwellings, all doors having been shut; and a certain woman, having withdrawn from the grinding because of fear, will use a most thin voice like a most slender bird; and all grinding women will fall to the ground, and cities and their blood-stained rulers, awaiting the punishment from above, upon the occasion of a most bitter and bloody time, like a blossoming almond tree and continuous punishments pressing upon them, like a multitude of locusts descending, and the lawless ones being cast off, like black and contemptible caper berries. And the good man will go to his eternal house rejoicing; but the worthless ones, beating themselves, will fill all their things with lamentation, and neither stored-up silver nor tested gold will be useful any longer. For a great blow will possess everything, until a water-jar standing by some spring, and a wheel of a vehicle, which might happen to be left in the hollow after ceasing, a time of circuit, and the one passing through the water of life of the laver-age. And of humans lying on the earth there is one salvation, if their souls might recognize them, and might turn back toward him by whom also they have been generated.

lemmas.gloss: grinding, millstone (context: the act of grinding)
bath-bearing, nuptial; here used of an age/era

choices.why: Context of women ceasing work and a woman withdrawing from it fits the Qohelet 12:3-4 imagery of grinding women; 'the grinding' captures the activity, not the stone.
Literal rendering of the compound adjective + noun; preserves the cosmic guardian imagery tied to the 'higher powers' being shaken.
Compound μιάσμα (pollution/blood) + φόνος (murder); 'blood-stained' matches the visceral sense of rulers stained by bloodshed.
Direct simile; the almond tree blossoming white signals the white hair of old age and the sudden arrival of judgment in the Qohelet tradition.
rejected: like an almond tree in bloom

choices.why: Loutron = bath/laver, phoros = bearing; the phrase likely signifies the baptismal era or the age of washing; 'laver-age' keeps the compound force without over-interpretation.
Reflexive 'themselves' (αὐτῶν) with souls as subject; the souls recognize the persons they belong to, a moment of self-knowledge before God.

bible_refs.note: Fear God before the evil days come; sun, moon, stars darkened; mighty men cease; grinding women cease; doors shut; voice of bird; almond blossoms; grasshopper burden; caper berry; silver/gold useless; water jar broken at spring, wheel broken at cistern; dust returns to earth, spirit returns to God.
The sun shall be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and terrible day of the Lord.
Sun darkened, moon not giving light, stars falling, powers of heavens shaken.
Sun becomes black, moon like blood, stars fall, sky vanishes, mountains and islands moved.
Fear God and keep his commandments; God will bring every deed into judgment.

pass_b_english: One must still fear God while young, before handing oneself over to evils, before the great and terrible day of God arrives. On that day the sun will no longer shine, nor the moon, nor the other stars. The higher powers, the world-guarding angels, will be shaken in that universal winter and turmoil. Mighty men will cease their labors, and working women will cease as well, retreating into the dark recesses of their houses with all doors shut. A woman who has withdrawn from the grinding because of fear will use a voice as thin as the slenderest bird. All impure women will fall to the ground, and cities together with their blood-stained rulers will await punishment from above when the most bitter and bloody time comes, like a blossoming almond tree, and successive punishments press on like swarms of locusts descending. The lawless will be cast aside like a black and contemptible caper berry. The good man will go rejoicing to his eternal home, but the wicked, beating their breasts, will fill everything that is theirs, and neither stored-up silver nor tested gold will be of any further use. For a great blow will seize everything, as far as the water jar standing by a spring, and the cart-wheel left in the hollow, the time of its circuit having ceased, and life through water, once the laver-bearing age has passed. The only salvation for human beings lying on the earth is if their souls would come to know him and fly up to the one from whom they were also born.
notes: The phrase 'ἀνθοῦντος ἀμυγδάλου' (blossoming almond) follows the LXX of Ecclesiastes 12:5. The 'λουτροφόρου αἰῶνος' (laver-age) is a unique Christian adaptation of the 'cistern/wheel' imagery (Eccl 12:6), likely referring to the baptismal era. The final clause about souls recognizing themselves and turning to their Creator is a Christian theological expansion on Eccl 12:7.

problems.quote: All noble women will fall to the ground
problems.why: ἄναγνοι means impure or unchaste, not noble. The English reverses the moral sense.
problems.fix: All impure women will fall to the ground

problems.quote: if their souls might recognize them and turn back to the one
problems.source_quote: εἰ ἐπιγνοῖεν αὐτῶν αἱ ψυχαὶ, καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀναπταῖεν
problems.why: αὐτῶν belongs to 'souls', so 'them' wrongly supplies an object. ἀναπταῖεν means 'fly up', not 'turn back'. The object of recognition is God.
problems.fix: if their souls would come to know him and fly up to the one by whom they were born.

problems.quote: the wicked will beat their breasts over all they possess
problems.source_quote: οἱ δέ γε φαῦλοι, πάντα τὰ αὐτῶν ἐμπλήσουσι κοπτόμενοι
problems.why: ἐμπλήσουσι means they will fill all that is theirs while mourning; the filling is lost.
problems.fix: The wicked, beating their breasts, will fill everything that is theirs.
problems.ruling: ἐμπλήσουσι ('will fill') with πάντα τὰ αὐτῶν is dropped. The Greek has them fill all their things while lamenting (κοπτόμενοι), not beat their breasts over possessions.

problems.quote: until the water jar standing by some spring is shattered
problems.source_quote: καὶ μέχρις ὑδρίας ἑστώσης πρός τινι κρήνῃ
problems.why: The blow reaches as far as the jar still standing; nothing says it is shattered.
problems.fix: A great blow will seize everything, as far as the water jar standing by a spring.
problems.ruling: μέχρις ὑδρίας ἑστώσης says the blow reaches even the jar still standing by a spring. 'Is shattered' is an addition and reverses the sense.

problems.quote: and the wheel of a vehicle that happens to be left in the hollow when the circling stops, and the course of the water of life has passed through the laver-age
problems.source_quote: καὶ τροχοῦ ὀχήματος, ὃν ἂν τύχῃ καταλελεῖφθαι ἐν τῷ κοιλώματι παυσαμένης, χρόνον τε περιδρομῆς, καὶ τῆς δι᾽ ὕδατος ζωῆς παροδεύσαντος τοῦ λουτροφόρου αἰῶνος
problems.why: The blow reaches wheel and life-through-water; the laver-bearing age passes, and the circuit-time is dropped and reassigned.
problems.fix: as far as the cart-wheel left in the hollow, the time of its circuit having ceased, and life through water, once the laver-bearing age has passed.
problems.ruling: τοῦ λουτροφόρου αἰῶνος is the subject of the genitive absolute παροδεύσαντος. The English makes 'course of the water of life' the subject and garbles the syntax and referents. χρόνον τε περιδρομῆς is also reassigned.

edits.new: All impure women will fall to the ground

fixed: Corrected 'All noble women' to 'All impure women' to match ἄναγνοι (impure/unchaste).
Fixed recognition object and 'turn back' to 'fly up': souls recognize God (αὐτῶν = his) and ἀναπταῖεν means fly up.
Restored 'fill everything that is theirs' from ἐμπλήσουσι πάντα τὰ αὐτῶν; 'beat their breasts' is the participle κοπτόμενοι.

Removed 'is shattered' (not in source) and restructured the final clause to follow the Greek series: the blow reaches as far as the jar, the wheel, the circuit-time, and the laver-bearing age passing.

last_rejected.quote: come to know him and fly up to the one
last_rejected.source_quote: εἰ ἐπιγνοῖεν αὐτῶν αἱ ψυχαί, καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀναπταῖεν
last_rejected.why: ἐπιγνοῖεν has no object; αὐτὸν is only the goal of the ascent.
last_rejected.fix: if their souls come to know, and fly up to him by whom they were also born
last_rejected.ruling: Greek ἐπιγνοῖεν takes an implicit object; the English supplies 'him', which is the natural referent given 'πρὸς αὐτὸν ... ὑφ᾽ οὗ'. Within normal translation range, not a meaning change.
